183.english_meaning: Remaining the same in all cases and at all times; consistent.
183.example: Assume the earth to be a sphere of uniform density.

183.english_meaning: Not influenced or affected by something else.
183.example: Acceleration due to gravity is independent of the mass of the body.

183.english_meaning: The energy held by an object because of its position relative to other objects.
183.example: The formula is used to calculate the difference of potential energy between two points.

183.english_meaning: Relating to the path followed by an object moving around a star, planet, or moon.
183.example: What would be its orbital size as compared to that of the earth?

183.english_meaning: The movement of an object in a circular or elliptical course around another object.
183.example: How long will a star take to complete one revolution?

183.english_meaning: Relating to the force that attracts a body toward the center of the earth or any other physical body having mass.
183.example: The energy required to launch a satellite out of earth's gravitational influence.

183.english_meaning: The capacity to have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of someone or something.
183.example: The satellite must escape the earth's gravitational influence.

183.english_meaning: The minimum speed needed for an object to break free from the gravitational attraction of a massive body.
183.example: Does the escape speed of a body depend on the mass of the body?

183.english_meaning: Having the shape of an ellipse; oval.
183.example: A comet orbits the sun in a highly elliptical orbit.

183.english_meaning: The quantity of rotation of a body, which is the product of its moment of inertia and its angular velocity.
183.example: Does the comet have a constant angular momentum throughout its orbit?

183.english_meaning: To cause pain or suffering to; to affect or trouble.
183.example: Which of the following symptoms is likely to afflict an astronaut in space?

183.english_meaning: Relating to the determination of the relative position of something.
183.example: The astronaut suffered from an orientational problem in zero gravity.

183.english_meaning: Relating to or shaped like a hemisphere (half of a sphere).
183.example: The gravitational intensity at the centre of a hemispherical shell.

183.english_meaning: Based on random choice or personal whim, rather than any reason or system.
183.example: The direction of the gravitational intensity at an arbitrary point P.

184.english_meaning: The force that attracts a body toward the center of the earth or toward any other physical body having mass.
184.example: Gravitation is the fundamental force that keeps planets in their orbits.

184.english_meaning: Remaining the same in all cases and at all times; consistent.
184.example: The sphere is assumed to have a uniform mass density throughout its volume.

184.english_meaning: The degree of compactness of a substance, defined as mass per unit volume.
184.example: The density of the material determines how much it weighs for a given size.

184.english_meaning: In a direction at right angles to the horizon; straight up or down.
184.example: The rocket was fired vertically into the sky.

184.english_meaning: An object thrown into the air with great force.
184.example: The escape speed of a projectile depends on the mass of the planet.

184.english_meaning: The minimum speed needed for an object to break free from the gravitational attraction of a massive body.
184.example: The escape speed from Earth is approximately 11.2 km/s.

184.english_meaning: An artificial body placed in orbit around the earth or moon or another planet.
184.example: The satellite orbits the earth at a constant height.

184.english_meaning: Spent or used up (a resource such as energy or money).
184.example: A large amount of energy must be expended to launch the satellite.

184.english_meaning: The power to have an effect on someone or something.
184.example: The satellite must be moved out of the earth's gravitational influence.

184.english_meaning: So small or unimportant as to be not worth considering.
184.example: At that distance, the initial speeds of the stars were negligible.

184.english_meaning: An instance of one moving object or person striking violently against another.
184.example: The two stars are moving toward a head-on collision.

184.english_meaning: Not changed from the original shape or form.
184.example: Assume the stars remain undistorted until the moment of impact.

184.english_meaning: The amount of work needed to move a unit charge or mass from a reference point to a specific point in a field.
184.example: We need to calculate the gravitational potential at the midpoint.

184.english_meaning: A state in which opposing forces or influences are balanced.
184.example: The object is in equilibrium when the net force acting on it is zero.

184.english_meaning: Not likely to change or fail; firmly established.
184.example: We must determine if the equilibrium of the object is stable or unstable.

48.english_meaning: The inverse of a number or a quantity, obtained by dividing 1 by that number.
48.hindi_meaning: व्युत्क्रम (एक संख्या जिसे 1 को उस संख्या से भाग देकर प्राप्त किया जाता है)

48.english_meaning: Marked by exactness and accuracy of expression or detail.
48.example: We need a more precise measurement for this experiment.

48.english_meaning: Coming between two things in time, place, order, or character.
48.hindi_meaning: मध्यवर्ती (दो अवस्थाओं या चरणों के बीच का)
48.example: Always keep extra digits in intermediate steps to avoid rounding errors.

48.english_meaning: The powers to which base quantities are raised to express a physical quantity.
48.hindi_meaning: विमाएँ (वे घातें जो किसी भौतिक राशि को व्यक्त करने के लिए मूल राशियों पर चढ़ाई जाती हैं)
48.example: The dimensions of volume are expressed in terms of length.

48.english_meaning: Serving as a basic or foundational part; primary or essential.
48.example: Mass, length, and time are fundamental quantities in mechanics.

48.english_meaning: Relating to the branch of physics concerned with heat and temperature and their relation to energy and work.
48.example: Thermodynamic temperature is measured in Kelvin.

48.english_meaning: Emitting or reflecting light, shining brightly.
48.example: Luminous intensity is one of the base quantities in SI units.

48.english_meaning: A quantity representing the power to which a given number or expression is to be raised.
48.example: Base quantities are raised to certain exponents in a dimensional formula.

48.english_meaning: Free from outside control; not depending on another for its value or state.
48.example: The volume of an object is independent of mass and time.

48.english_meaning: The great size or extent of something, or a numerical quantity.
48.example: In dimensional representation, the numerical magnitudes are not considered.

48.english_meaning: Equal in value, amount, function, meaning, etc.
48.example: Initial velocity and final velocity are equivalent in terms of their dimensions.

48.english_meaning: An expression showing which base quantities represent the dimensions of a physical quantity.
48.hindi_meaning: विमीय सूत्र (वह व्यंजक जो यह दर्शाता है कि मूल राशियाँ किसी भौतिक राशि की विमा को कैसे व्यक्त करती हैं)
48.example: The dimensional formula of speed is [M0 L T-1].

48.english_meaning: An equation obtained by equating a physical quantity with its dimensional formula.
48.hindi_meaning: विमीय समीकरण (किसी भौतिक राशि को उसके विमीय सूत्र के बराबर रखने पर प्राप्त समीकरण)
48.example: The dimensional equation of force is written as [F] = [M L T–2].

48.english_meaning: Representing one thing as equal to another.
48.example: Equating the physical quantity with its dimensional formula gives the dimensional equation.

48.english_meaning: Advice or information aimed at resolving a problem or difficulty.
48.example: Dimensional formulae are provided in the appendix for your guidance.
